1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; IAM: Identity and Access Management; CLI: command line interface; EMR: Elastic MapReduce; ACL: access control list; MFA: multi-factor authentication; SDK: software development kit; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; ECS: Elastic Container Service; EKS: Elastic Kubernetes Service; STS: Security Token Service; KMS: Key Management Service; RDS: Relational Database Service; SQS: Simple Queue Service; NAT: network address translation; MSK: Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka; ETL: extract, transform, load; TCP: Transmission Control Protocol; SSO: single sign-on; ENI: elastic network interface

  • Update VPC security groups so only the right sources reach data stores
  • Create and update IAM groups, roles, endpoints and services
  • Create and rotate credentials with AWS Secrets Manager
  • Set up IAM roles for Lambda, API Gateway, the AWS CLI and CloudFormation
  • Apply IAM policies to roles, endpoints and services (S3 Access Points, AWS PrivateLink)
  • Describe managed versus unmanaged services
  • Use domains, domain units and projects in SageMaker Unified Studio

Authentication proves who or what you are. Authorization (Module 15) decides what you may do.

2Network Access: VPC Security Groups (skill 4.1.1)

Running case

Kestrel Freight Locks the Doors

  • The Redshift cluster is reachable from the whole internet
  • A Glue job cannot connect to the billing database
  • An analyst keeps a database password in a script
  • Your job: authenticate every caller and open only the paths that are needed

  • A security group is a virtual firewall at the resource level (network interface): allow rules only, stateful (return traffic is allowed automatically), default deny for inbound
  • Update rules to least access: allow only the needed port and source: Redshift 5439, PostgreSQL 5432, MySQL 3306, HTTPS 443; use another security group as the source (for example the Glue job's) instead of an IP range; never open 0.0.0.0/0 to a data store
  • Glue, EMR and Lambda in a VPC: Glue connections use security groups with a self-referencing inbound rule (the group allows traffic from itself) so the job's workers can talk to each other
  • Network ACLs are stateless subnet-level filters (allow and deny rules) and are not the main control for data stores
  • Private connectivity: VPC endpoints (below) keep traffic off the internet; place data stores in private subnets
Exam tip

"Allow a Glue job to reach a private database" → a database security group rule that allows the job's security group (and the right port), not a public IP range.

3IAM Identities: Groups, Roles, Endpoints and Services (skills 4.1.2 and 4.1.4)

Identity Use Remember
IAM user A person or app with long-term credentials Avoid for workloads; use MFA
IAM group Collection of users sharing permissions Attach policies to the group, not each user
IAM role An identity with no long-term credentials that a trusted entity assumes to get temporary credentials Preferred for services, applications and cross-account access
Trust policy Who may assume the role Separate from the permissions policy (what the role may do)
Service-linked role A role predefined for an AWS service Created and managed by the service
Federation (IAM Identity Center) People sign in with corporate identities and get temporary role access Best for human access to many accounts

IAM roles for services and tools (skill 4.1.4)

Caller Role setup
AWS Lambda An execution role (trust: lambda.amazonaws.com) with permissions to the data stores and CloudWatch Logs
AWS Glue jobs and crawlers A Glue service role that can read the sources, write the targets, use the Data Catalog and the temp bucket
Amazon API Gateway IAM authorization for callers; an integration role so the API can call Lambda, Step Functions or other services
AWS CLI and SDKs Assume a role (named profile, IAM Identity Center sign-in, or environment) to get temporary credentials; never embed long-term keys
AWS CloudFormation A service role that CloudFormation assumes to create resources, so deployers need fewer direct permissions
Amazon EC2 / ECS / EKS Instance profile or task / pod role
Redshift, EMR, Step Functions, SageMaker Roles attached to the cluster or state machine (for example the Redshift IAM role used by COPY, UNLOAD and Spectrum)
  • Cross-account access: the data owner's role trusts the other account; the caller assumes the role (STS AssumeRole)

Endpoints

  • A VPC endpoint lets resources in your VPC reach AWS services privately: gateway endpoints (S3 and DynamoDB; a route table entry; no extra charge) and interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink: an elastic network interface with a private IP for many services, including your own)
  • Update endpoints to add services, route tables, subnets and security groups, and endpoint policies
Exam tip

"A Lambda function needs to read S3 and write Kinesis without long-term keys" → an IAM execution role with those permissions. "Keep S3 traffic off the internet" → a gateway VPC endpoint.

4Secrets: Creating and Rotating Credentials (skill 4.1.3)

  • AWS Secrets Manager stores, retrieves and rotates database credentials, API keys and tokens; secrets are encrypted with AWS KMS; access is controlled by IAM
  • Applications fetch the secret at run time, so no password lives in code, job parameters or configuration files
  • Rotation: automatic rotation on a schedule (rate() or cron()); managed rotation (no Lambda to write) for Amazon RDS and Aurora master user credentials and the Redshift admin password; other secrets use a Lambda rotation function (created from a template or your own) that must reach both Secrets Manager and the database over the network
  • Rotation steps (create new secret version, set it in the database, test, finish) keep the old version available until the switch, so applications do not break
  • AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store also holds configuration and secrets (SecureString, encrypted with KMS) but has no built-in rotation (Module 15)
  • Glue connections and Redshift can reference a secret instead of a password
Exam tip

"Rotate the RDS password automatically and have applications keep working" → Secrets Manager rotation (managed for RDS and Aurora).

5Applying IAM Policies to Roles, Endpoints and Services (skill 4.1.5)

  • Identity-based policy: attached to a user, group or role; says what it may do
  • Resource-based policy: attached to a resource (S3 bucket, KMS key, SQS queue, Lambda function, secret); names a principal (including other accounts)
  • VPC endpoint policy: a resource policy on the endpoint that limits which principals and actions can use it (for example only your bucket)
  • Amazon S3 Access Points: named network endpoints for a bucket, each with its own access point policy (and optionally restricted to one VPC): they simplify permissions for shared datasets (give each team or application its own access point instead of one huge bucket policy)
  • AWS PrivateLink: private connectivity to a service (AWS, a partner or your own) over interface endpoints, no internet gateway, NAT or public IP; combine with endpoint policies
  • Evaluation: an explicit deny wins; otherwise something must allow; same-account access needs an allow in either the identity or the resource policy, cross-account needs both (Module 15)
  • Condition keys such as aws:SourceVpce (the endpoint) and aws:PrincipalOrgID restrict access to a VPC endpoint or your organization
Exam tip

"Allow only requests from the company's VPC endpoint to read a bucket" → a bucket policy (or access point policy) with an aws:SourceVpce condition, plus the endpoint.

6Managed versus Unmanaged Services (skill 4.1.6)

Managed services Unmanaged (self-managed) services
Examples RDS, Aurora, Redshift, DynamoDB, Glue, Athena, EMR Serverless, MSK, OpenSearch Service A database installed on EC2, a self-built Kafka or Hadoop cluster
AWS manages Hardware, host and often the engine software, patching, backups, high availability, scaling options Only the underlying infrastructure
You manage Data, access control, network settings, configuration, encryption choices The operating system, patches, engine upgrades, backups, high availability, security hardening
Trade-off Less operational work; less control Full control; much more work and risk
  • This is the shared responsibility model: AWS secures the cloud; you secure what you put in it; the more managed the service, the more AWS handles
  • Prefer managed (or serverless) services for least operational overhead and built-in security features such as automatic patching, backups and encryption
Exam tip

"Least operational overhead" almost always points to a managed or serverless service.

7SageMaker Unified Studio: Domains, Domain Units and Projects (skill 4.1.7)Verify live

  • Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is a single workspace for data, analytics and AI (notebooks, SQL, visual ETL, catalog, and generative AI help)
  • Domain: the top-level container for an organization's users, groups, projects, catalog and settings; an administrator creates it and manages who can sign in (for example through IAM Identity Center)
  • Domain units: hierarchy under a domain to model business units or teams; owners set policies for the projects in their unit; if none exist, everything sits at the root domain
  • Projects: the collaboration boundary where members work on a business use case with shared data, compute and tools; members have roles (owner, contributor) and access depends on authorization policies
  • Why it matters for security: who may create projects, who is a member, and which data a project may see are controlled at these levels, and the business catalog (Module 7) and data sharing (Module 18) follow the same structure
Exam tip

"Separate teams or business units with their own policies and projects inside one governed workspace" → SageMaker Unified Studio domain units and projects.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1A Glue job runs in a VPC and must connect to a private Amazon Redshift cluster. What is the most secure network setting?

  • AAllow 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5439 in the Redshift security group so that every client can connect
  • BIn the Redshift security group, allow inbound TCP 5439 from the Glue job's security group
  • CMake the Redshift cluster publicly accessible and let the job reach it through its public address
  • DDisable the security group on the cluster's network interface
Show the answer

Answer: B. Referencing the job's security group as the source opens only the needed port to only that resource.

S2The database password for an Amazon RDS instance must be rotated automatically without breaking applications, and the team does not want to write code. What should be used?

  • AA Systems Manager Parameter Store String parameter
  • BAWS Secrets Manager with managed rotation
  • CA password in an S3 object
  • DA manually updated environment variable
Show the answer

Answer: B. Secrets Manager rotates RDS and Aurora master credentials on a schedule with managed rotation, and applications fetch the current secret at run time.

S3Which description of managed versus unmanaged services is correct?

  • AWith a managed database service AWS patches the engine and runs backups and failover; the customer manages data and access
  • BWith a database on EC2 AWS patches the database engine for the customer
  • CManaged services remove all of the customer's security responsibility
  • DUnmanaged services give the least operational overhead of all options
Show the answer

Answer: A. Managed services shift infrastructure and software maintenance to AWS; the customer is still responsible for data, access and configuration.

S4Several teams share one SageMaker Unified Studio domain. The company wants each business unit to set its own policies for who can create projects. Which feature provides this?

  • ADomain units
  • BA single root project
  • CS3 lifecycle rules
  • DSecurity groups
Show the answer

Answer: A. Domain units model business-unit hierarchies, and their owners set policies for the projects in their unit.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Security groups Stateful, allow-only, default deny inbound; allow specific port and source security group; ports 5439 / 5432 / 3306 / 443; Glue self-referencing rule; never 0.0.0.0/0 to data stores
IAM identities Roles (temporary credentials, trust + permissions policy) for services; groups for users; IAM Identity Center for people; STS AssumeRole for cross-account
Role setups Lambda execution role, Glue service role, API Gateway integration role and IAM auth, CLI assume role/SSO, CloudFormation service role, Redshift/EMR/Step Functions roles
Endpoints Gateway (S3, DynamoDB; route table; free) vs interface/PrivateLink (ENI, private IP); endpoint policies
Secrets Manager Stores/rotates credentials, KMS encrypted; managed rotation for RDS/Aurora master and Redshift admin; Lambda rotation otherwise; Parameter Store no built-in rotation
Policies Identity vs resource vs endpoint policy; S3 Access Points (own policy, optional VPC-only); PrivateLink; conditions aws:SourceVpce; explicit deny wins
Managed vs unmanaged Managed = AWS runs infrastructure and software; you own data, access, configuration; least overhead = managed/serverless
SageMaker Unified Studio Domain (top) → domain units (business units, policies) → projects (collaboration, members, roles)
